body.p: Cuckoo. A mother and her children lived in some place. She had four children.[ShA:] The title is present in the publication, but is absent in the recording. One day the mother said to her children: "Children, children, bring me some water." The older child said: "I don't want." She says to the other one: "Bring me some water." The other said: "Take it yourself." She says to the other child. The other replies: "I'm sick." She said to the fourth child: "Bring some water for me, my child." "Stand up and get it!" The mother thought and thought for a long time, then a nose appeared out of her thimble, then wings [ShA:] Oblique destinative forms pujazoda and tÉzoda are unexpected here. Code-switching to Russian was appeared out of her broom, then before she knew it, she said: "Coo-coo" and flew up.improved for Enets in the publication, and I take the publication version here.. Then the children cried, shouting: "Mom, we'll help you, just come, we'll bring you water, we'll do everything for you, we will help you, just come, come, mom, come. She cries out loudly: "I don't need water now, I have a lot of water, I'll get water myself." The children were left crying like that, she became a cuckoo like that.
